claims.text: After MI, ACE inhibitors/ARBs reduce mortality, especially with anterior MI, LVEF ≤ 40%, HTN or diabetes;
claims.quote: Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs) reduce mortality risk in patients with myocardial infarction, especially in those with anterior infarction, left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 40%, hypertension, or diabetes (1).
claims.locator: Other Medications for Post-acute Treatment of Acute Coronary Syndrome

claims.text: given > 24 hours after thrombolysis stabilization and may be continued long-term.
claims.quote: ACE inhibitors and ARBs are given > 24 hours after thrombolysis stabilization and, because of continued beneficial effect, may be prescribed long-term.
claims.locator: Other Medications for Post-acute Treatment of Acute Coronary Syndrome

claims.text: Lisinopril in acute MI (hemodynamically stable, within 24 hours): 5 mg, 5 mg after 24 hours, 10 mg after 48 hours, then 10 mg daily
claims.quote: In hemodynamically stable patients within 24 hours of the onset of symptoms of acute myocardial infarction, give Zestril 5 mg orally, followed by 5 mg after 24 hours, 10 mg after 48 hours and then 10 mg once daily.
claims.locator: 2.3 Reduction of Mortality in Acute Myocardial Infarction

claims.quote: Dosing should continue for at least six weeks.
claims.locator: 2.3 Reduction of Mortality in Acute Myocardial Infarction

claims.text: Lisinopril: K-sparing diuretics raise hyperkalemia risk;
claims.quote: Potassium-sparing diuretics (spironolactone, amiloride, triamterene, and others) can increase the risk of hyperkalemia.

claims.text: NSAIDs raise renal-impairment risk and blunt the BP effect;
claims.quote: NSAIDS: Increased risk of renal impairment and loss of antihypertensive efficacy ( 7.3 )

claims.text: lithium toxicity has been reported (monitor lithium levels);
claims.quote: Lithium toxicity has been reported in patients receiving lithium concomitantly with drugs, which cause elimination of sodium, including ACE inhibitors.
Zestril is contraindicated in combination with a neprilysin inhibitor (e.g., sacubitril).

claims.text: Lisinopril overdose: hypotension is most likely, treated with IV normal saline;
claims.quote: The most likely manifestation of overdosage would be hypotension, for which the usual treatment would be intravenous infusion of normal saline solution.
